newsitem.title: ITALY: Eurotax to be repaid once Italy in EMU-Micheli.
newsitem.headline: Eurotax to be repaid once Italy in EMU-Micheli.

text.p: Italian cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli said there would not be another "Eurotax" and most of the current levy will be reimbursed to taxpayers once Italy joins European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"As it is known, 60 percent of this tax will be given back when Italy enters Europe and it is exclusively a one-off," Micheli said in an Italian television interview.

The government introduced the so-called Eurotax as a one-off levy on income taxes in the 1997 budget and is intended to raise 5.5 trillion lire in extra income this year and help get Italy's state accounts into shape for early EMU membership.
Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco has already said the government has no intention of carrying the Eurotax over into next year.
Micheli said he hoped the process of overhauling state accounts would result in interest rates "such as to make no longer necessary" enormous corrective measures like those taken in the past months.
